properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 10 at 5:01AM EDT by NWS Peachtree City GA
properties.description:
At 501 AM EDT, National Weather Service doppler radar indicated a
strong storm within a tropical rain band over McKibben, or near
Jackson, moving northwest at 50 mph.

HAZARD...Enhanced risk of a brief tornado.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Storms embedded within a tropical rainband have exhibited
localized rotation. A brief tornado could quickly form.

Locations impacted include...
McDonough, Jackson, Stockbridge, Hampton, Lovejoy, Locust Grove,
Jenkinsburg, Blacksville, Ola, Walker Mill, McKibben, Luella,
Flippen, Indian Springs State Park, and Kelleytown.
properties.instruction: People outdoors should seek shelter immediately.

properties.areaDesc: Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast; Santa Barbara County Southeastern Coast
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 10 at 1:57AM PDT until October 13 at 2:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor tidal overflow flooding is expected. Dangerous
rip currents and breaking waves due to elevated surf expected.

* WHERE...Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast and Santa
Barbara County Southeastern Coast.

* WHEN...From Saturday morning through Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Pooling of sea water is possible around high tide at
beach and harbor areas that is uncommon with normal tidal
ranges. Enhanced beach erosion is also possible. The risk for
significant damage is very low. There is an increased risk of
ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out
to sea. Waves can wash people off beaches and rocks, and
capsize small boats nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides of 6.6 to 7.2 feet will be
common each morning, with large secondary high tides in the
evening hours.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.areaDesc: Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued October 10 at 1:57AM PDT until October 11 at 3:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For vulnerable south-facing beaches, like Avalon and
Pebbly Beach, damaging sea-water flooding is likely. For all
other beaches and harbors, minor coastal flooding is expected.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands.

* WHEN...Until 3 PM PDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...For vulnerable south-facing beaches, sea-water
flooding can damage beach roads and structures, especially
around the time of high tide. For all other beaches and
harbors, shallow and minor sea-water flooding can impact
beaches and walkways. For all beach areas, significant erosion
is expected. There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Sunday carries the widest range of
coastal flooding outcomes due to chances of rain, wind, low
pressure tidal enhancements, and swells from multiple
directions. Coastal flooding impacts on Sunday could be
similar to other days, or greatly enhanced. High tides of 7.3
to 7.6 feet will be common each morning. This warning may be
extended past Sunday, or converted to a Coastal Flood Advisory
through Tuesday.
properties.instruction:
Stay off of beaches and coastal walkways, roads, and structures.
Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.
Heed advice from local officials.

properties.areaDesc: South Walton; Coastal Bay
properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued October 10 at 4:52AM EDT until October 11 at 11:00AM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of
2 to 14 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...South Walton and Coastal Bay Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 11 AM CDT this
morning. For the High Surf Warning, until 10 AM CDT Sunday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Breaking waves can sweep
people off jetties and docks, and into dangerous seas. Life-
threatening swimming conditions and significant beach erosion
can be expected. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers
away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor to locally moderate coastal flooding
will continue through today.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.
